headline: Argentine Dollar Hits High and Country Risk Rises to 831 Points Amid U.S. Election
summary: The retail exchange rate for the US dollar in Argentina rose for a second consecutive day to 1,570 pesos at Banco Nación, while country risk climbed to 831 points and stocks and bonds traded negatively in Wall Street.
why: Argentina's financial markets are highly volatile and sensitive to domestic policy developments as well as international political shifts such as U.S. elections.

impacts.name: Argentine Peso
impacts.why: Increased dollarization demand and rising country risk weaken the local currency.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Investor anxiety surrounding international election outcomes and local asset sell-offs drove capital flight into the US dollar and spiked sovereign risk spreads.
